- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is trending up, reduce upward bias — model tends to over-forecast after spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50) and forecast is trending down, reduce downward bias — model tends to under-forecast after sharp drops.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (prices moving back toward 65–70 range), model often overshoots in either direction — apply dampening to extremes.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates early drops or late rallies — adjust for lagged sentiment momentum (e.g., if sentiment turned negative 3–5 days ago, reduce forecast slope).
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.67 → -0.50 → +0.67), model tends to misread momentum — use sentiment smoothing or lagged sentiment weights.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment confirms — if sentiment is flat or mixed, model should not assume strong directional bias.
